required_floor_classes.lane_definition: A defense scenario cannot pass if treaty commitments, mission coverage, geographic posture, or essential defense services are reduced below reviewed floors without explicit policy selection and risk review.
A defense scenario cannot pass if lower costs are achieved by degrading readiness, personnel safety, training quality, maintenance quality, or operational risk controls below reviewed floors.
A defense scenario cannot pass if transition burdens, base closures, personnel losses, reserve effects, contractor displacement, or family impacts are shifted without explicit distributional review.
A defense scenario cannot pass if strategic reserve, munitions depth, sealift/airlift capacity, cyber resilience, industrial-base capacity, or surge capacity falls below reviewed floors.

A defense scenario cannot pass without a specific force structure, procurement schedule, transition plan, legal authority, implementation cost, contract-management model, and adverse-realization stress path.

defense_specific_floor_definitions.definition: Treaty and statutory defense commitments require explicit mission, posture, and risk review before any lower-cost scenario can pass.
Readiness requires sourced force, training, maintenance, availability, and mission-capable measures before any lower-cost scenario can pass.
Personnel safety, operating tempo, family impact, and transition risk require explicit review before any scenario can pass.
Strategic reserve, munitions, industrial-base, mobility, cyber, and surge capacity require explicit sourced floors.
Force structure, procurement schedule, contract management, and transition feasibility require explicit policy design and sourced values.

public_warning_phrases: This defense floor packet defines required floor concepts, but it does not set threshold values or pass/fail findings.

No defense lower-cost scenario is admissible until treaty commitments, readiness, personnel safety, strategic reserve, force structure, procurement, equity, and delivery-feasibility floors are thresholded, sourced, reviewed, and passed.
A GDP policy band is not a force-structure plan, procurement schedule, federal score, target cost, or solver input.
No target cost, federal effect, gross savings, net savings, solver input, department-cut instruction, technology-savings claim, or balanced-budget claim is populated.
No FOIA request, records request, form, email, phone call, or agency/person contact was submitted.

This record is not outcome-floor passage, not a force-structure plan, not a procurement schedule, not a federal score, not a target-cost selection, not solver input, not a solver run, not a rate calculation, not a public rate card, not a tax proposal, not a savings estimate, not a waste finding, not a fraud finding, not a department-cut instruction, not a technology-savings claim, and not a balanced-budget claim.
